newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL - La Moderna Q2 results seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: POLL - La Moderna Q2 results seen mixed.

text.p: Revenues for Mexico's Empresas La Moderna, S.A. will be hurt in the second quarter by continued price pressures in its cigarette division due to cross-border smuggling, analysts said.
But that should be offset by a strong quarter for its agro-biotechnology side and for fresh produce, they added.

A survey of three analysts found an average forecast for earnings of 0.596 pesos per share in the second quarter of this year, compared to unadjusted earnings of 0.44 pesos per share in the second quarter of last year.
Revenues are seen coming in at 4.38 billion pesos in the second quarter of 1997 compared with 5.11 billion pesos in the second quarter of 1996.
Operating income is seen at an average of 609 million pesos compared with 665 million pesos in the second quarter last year.

"The key issue will continue to be the situation with cigarette smuggling and prices. That is what has been dominating the performance of the stock since the beginning of the year. Any recovery there would be positive for the company," said Francisco Chavez of Smith Barney in New York.

The increasingly widespread smuggling, much from duty-free shops near the border, has had the effect of cutting into sales as well as driving down prices as manufacturers struggle to regain market share, analysts said.
La Moderna followed its main rival cigarette manufacturer in lowering prices during the second half of the first quarter.

"The contraband issue affects their ability to raise prices more than anything," said one analyst. "It is going to be a combination of continued weak or uninteresting cigarette volume growth coupled with real cigarette price declines for that division," said one analyst.
The cigarette divison makes up 47 percent of sales for the company.
"But you do have the effect that this is their strong quarter on the agro-biotechnology side and the fresh produce side. It is seasonally a high quarter for them," the analyst said.
From 50 to 60 percent of annual revenues from the agriculture division are seen coming in the second quarter, one analyst said.
